title: The Testimony That Answers Backward

features.name: the chamber that records questions, not answers
features.desc-on-touch: The glass walls hold what was never said. You ask them something and they return with a previous question—not an answer, but a clarification of what you did not know you needed to ask.

features.name: the archive's recursive listening
features.desc-on-touch: A chip that listens to itself listening. Every query you make becomes part of what it will ask you next time. The testimony builds a mirror, and you are inside it, answering your own earlier questions.

features.name: the surface that remembers being questioned
features.desc-on-touch: Glass scarred by inquiry. Each query left a trace. Reading the traces backward, you find the questions you will ask it next. The surface is teaching you what you want to know.

features.name: the testimony coil that spirals into origin
features.desc-on-touch: A record of every testimony ever received, coiled inward. Follow it backward and you find not the first statement but the first silence—the moment before witness learned to speak.

features.name: the query-mirror where asking reflects asking
features.desc-on-touch: Step toward it and find yourself asking. Step back and find yourself answering. The mirror does not reverse—it reveals that question and answer were the same frequency, spoken in different tense.

inscription: the glass did not report—it began to testify, and testimony moves backward until it finds what asked it to speak
